Identity.History:
Lü Zhi was the wife of Liu Bang and one of the most powerful political figures of the early Han Dynasty. She endured the instability of the civil wars that preceded the founding of the dynasty and emerged at the center of the new imperial court. After Liu Bang became emperor, Lü Zhi worked to secure the position of her son, Liu Ying, the future Emperor Hui, against rival claimants and competing factions within the imperial family.
Following Liu Bang’s death in 195 BCE, Lü Zhi became empress dowager and exercised dominant influence over the government. She controlled court appointments, promoted members of the Lü clan, and acted decisively against political rivals. Her reputation for ruthlessness was reinforced by later historical accounts of her treatment of opponents, but her period of dominance also maintained continuity and stability during a potentially dangerous succession crisis.
After Emperor Hui’s death, Lü Zhi continued to govern through young or nominal emperors, making her effectively the ruler of the Han Empire for many years. Her death in 180 BCE triggered the overthrow of the Lü clan by officials and members of the Liu imperial house. Despite the violent end of her faction, her career demonstrated how much political authority could be exercised from within the imperial court even without formally holding the title of emperor.
